Transparency & Timeline Notice

Dual Timelines: To maintain our immersive fictional universe while strictly complying with modern digital distribution standards, our catalog features two timelines: a fictional Narrative Era (e.g., 1987) tied to the band's lore, and a real-world Actual Release Date (e.g., 2026) reflecting when the audio was officially distributed to streaming platforms. Featured Release & Lore Spotlight // October 18, 2011
25 Years of "Ignition" (1986–2011) The Cosmic Tidal Lock Sound™

Starfield Calibration

Released Oct 18, 2011 • 25th Anniversary of "Ignition (The Forger's Call)" • 80s Cosmic Pop

Released on Tuesday, October 18, 2011—twenty-five years to the exact day after "Ignition (The Forger's Call)" first detonated inside The Crucible on Homecoming Saturday, October 18, 1986—Starfield Calibration is the band's silver-anniversary gift to Forger Nation while recharging from their exhausting 2004 post-Progress Street burnout.

Rather than rushing back onto a high-friction stadium tour before Ryan and Cassidy were ready, Chief Audio Architect Cassidy O'Connell retreated to the family's private Blacksburg studio to rebuild fourteen foundational tracks (1987–2001) entirely within The Cosmic Tidal Lock Sound™—including retrospective lyric updates celebrating their liberation from Apex Records' "Plastic Sky" and the first-ever finalized studio master of "Atmosphere" (rescuing the song from its rough 1992 early-90s Friction demo and bringing it back to the lush 1980s sound the band loves so much).

Listen to Starfield Calibration The Cosmic Tidal Lock Sound™ Explainer
While the Band Recharges, Holly Builds an Empire (1997 → 2011 → 2015)

To the outside world, the 2004–2014 Burnout Hiatus looked like a quiet retreat. Behind closed doors, CEO Holly O'Connell was executing an 18-year institutional wealth and liability blueprint she first conceived in 1997 during Hard Reset—when the "$13.99 War" and the 1996 "American Dream" Jackpot taught her that the family's capital and master catalog had to be ruthlessly siloed and diversified.

By the time Starfield Calibration dropped in October 2011, Holly had already stripped all operational liabilities out of Engine Room Records, LLC (2005), spun off Artists First Management, LLC and Stardust Strategic Assets, LLC (2005), built CPI barrier-free housing via Stardust Blacksburg, LLC (2007), and used the 2008–2010 financial crash to acquire Class-A Century City office towers for cash through Pacific Rim Properties, LLC (2009–2011)—laying the final bricks for The O'Connell Family Revocable Trust (2012) and the August 2015 Delaware Migration ($2.4B+ AUM).

2004 Pre-Hiatus Studio Milestone

Progress Street

1985 Origins • 2004 Studio Release • Blacksburg, VA

A roaring eleven-track 1980s AOR and stadium synth-rock homecoming. Named after Progress Street NE in Blacksburg—where Ryan, Cassidy, Holly, Evan, and Tyler lived in an off-campus rental house while attending Commonwealth Polytechnic Institute (CPI)—this record celebrates the unbreakable family bond that carried them from a basement upright piano to sold-out arenas.

Featuring the Fourth Quarter stadium stomper "Saturday Night Lights: The Crucible" (cleared under Holly's legendary 1986 $1.00 Perpetual Mutual Cross-License with CPI), the full-band AOR resurrection of "Empty Arenas," and their heartfelt pre-hiatus promise to Forger Nation, "Last Bus Home: Lights Out on Progress Street."

Explore Progress Street Stream & Read Lyrics
Driven Exclusively by Family • Class A CDL Certified

The Stardust Fleet: Rolling Sanctuary

For The Stardust Engine, accessibility and privacy are non-negotiable. Rather than leasing third-party tour buses or hiring outside drivers, Tyler Wright, Evan Wright, and Holly O'Connell all earned their Class A Commercial Driver's Licenses (with Passenger and Airbrake endorsements)—and the band commissioned two custom-engineered coaches built around Ryan's wheelchair.

45-FT INTERSTATE FLAGSHIP
2002 Custom High-Deck Motorcoach • Sainte-Claire, QC

Sainte-Claire 45H3 ("The Iron Horse")

Forged in Québec stainless steel with a bespoke Cosmic Nebula exterior wrap, The Iron Horse is the family's 54,000-lb coast-to-coast touring fortress. Engineered with a mid-ship 60-inch vertical hydraulic cassette lift, zero-threshold 38-inch interior corridors, five private family berths, and an onboard acoustic isolation lounge.

View Fleet Roster & Specs 2001 Québec Deal 2002 Delivery
30-FT LOW-FLOOR LAUNCH UNIT
2004 Restyled Low-Floor Diesel • Launch Customer

Prairie Coachworks RLFD30 ("Progress Street")

Immortalized on the cover of Progress Street, The Stardust Engine became Prairie Coachworks' very first launch customer for the restyled 30-foot low-floor coach. Built with a front-door-only executive layout and pneumatic kneeling suspension, it unfolds a simple 1:6 front flip-out ADA ramp right onto the Blacksburg curb so Ryan can roll aboard in seconds.
